mainTopic: Torah study, ברכות and immersion for a בעל קרי
overview: The גמרא first works out what רבי יהודה means in the משנה when he says a בעל קרי 'blesses.' It suggests he only means thinking the ברכות silently, but a ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה wants them said out loud. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that רבי יהודה treats these ברכות like הלכות דרך ארץ. A ברייתא then teaches that Torah must be learned with the awe of Sinai, so a בעל קרי is limited in learning. The תנאים argue about how far that limit goes. רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds that words of Torah, like fire, cannot become impure, and רב נחמן בר יצחק rules that practice follows him. The גמרא then discusses the immersion of a בעל קרי: pouring nine קבין instead of a full מקוה of forty סאה, the fence this immersion makes against sin, and immersing in hot bathhouses. רב דימי limits the nine-קבין leniency to a sick person with an involuntary emission. רבין then begins to report an incident in אושא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A plain בעל קרי is obligated to immerse, according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a proof that רבי יהודה exempts only a woman who saw נדה blood during relations from immersing, but does require a plain בעל קרי to immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who was having relations and saw נדה blood does not need to immerse, but someone who only had a seminal emission is obligated to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof it started earlier. It shows that רבי יהודה does require an ordinary בעל קרי to immerse, and it uses this to set up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה exempts the woman from immersing only because she is a נדה anyway, so immersing now would not make her טהור. A person who is only a בעל קרי has no such reason, so he must immerse. If רבי יהודה takes the impurity of קרי that seriously, it is hard to read the משנה as letting him say ברכות out loud.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has seen menstrual blood and is impure
Immersion in a מקוה to become pure
A man who had a seminal emission

phrases.english: A woman who was having relations and saw menstrual blood
does not need to immerse,
but one who only had a seminal emission is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל בַּעַל קֶרִי גְּרֵידָא — מְחַיַּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof begun before this section about רבי יהודה's view of a בעל קרי
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה requires a plain בעל קרי to immerse
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling that a woman who saw נדה blood during relations does not need to immerse

steps.title: Read 'he blesses' as 'he thinks the blessing'
steps.stepSummary: Because רבי יהודה requires a בעל קרי to immerse, the גמרא reads the משנה's word מברך as meaning מהרהר, thinking the ברכה in his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't read it as 'he says the blessing.' Read it as 'he thinks it in his mind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how we read רבי יהודה's words in the משנה. When he says a בעל קרי 'blesses,' it means he only thinks the ברכות silently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows from the proof in step 1. A person who still needs to immerse should not say ברכות out loud, so רבי יהודה must only allow הרהור. In this reading, רבי יהודה goes further than the תנא קמא only by allowing silent ברכות both before and after.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say, don't read it this way
Thinks it in his mind, without speaking

phrases.english: Don't say 'he recites a blessing,'
phrases.notes: This is the word רבי יהודה uses in the משנה: 'he blesses before and after.'

phrases.english: rather, 'he thinks it in his mind.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא ״מְבָרֵךְ״, אֶלָּא מְהַרְהֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof from step 1 to reread the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say the ברכות out loud
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה only lets him think the ברכות silently

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה wants the ברכות said out loud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the הרהור reading with a ברייתא. There רבי מאיר says a בעל קרי only thinks the ברכות, and רבי יהודה says he says them out loud in all cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יהודה even hold of thinking the ברכות? It was taught: a בעל קרי with no water to immerse says קריאת שמע but no ברכות before or after it. When he eats bread he says the ברכה after it but not before it. Where he cannot say a ברכה, he thinks it in his heart and does not say it, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: in both cases he says them out loud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 2. A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה does not use הרהור at all, because he says the ברכות are spoken out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, thinking in the heart is רבי מאיר's idea, and רבי יהודה disagrees with it. So it makes no sense to say that רבי יהודה's 'he blesses' in the משנה means 'he thinks.' The rereading from step 2 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Says it with his lips, out loud

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִרְהוּר?
phrases.english: And does רבי יהודה hold of thinking in the mind?
But wasn't it taught:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל קֶרִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַיִם לִטְבּוֹל —
phrases.english: A בעל קרי who has no water to immerse in
reads קריאת שמע but does not say the blessings,
neither before it nor after it.
And he eats his bread and says the blessing after it,
but does not say the blessing before it.
But he thinks it in his heart

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: and does not say it with his lips; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו.
phrases.english: Either way, he says them with his lips.
phrases.notes: 'Either way' covers both cases, the ברכות of שמע and the ברכות of the meal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִרְהוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading of מברך as מהרהר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that רבי יהודה means only הרהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, הרהור is רבי מאיר's view, and רבי יהודה says the ברכות are said out loud. So רבי יהודה cannot mean הרהור in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: In the ברייתא, רבי מאיר says to think the ברכות silently, while רבי יהודה says to say them out loud. This means רבי יהודה does not rely on הרהור.

steps.title: רבי יהודה treats these ברכות like הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say these ברכות out loud because he puts them in the same group as הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבי יהודה made them like the laws of proper conduct.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a new answer. רבי יהודה really does let a בעל קרי say the ברכות out loud, because he treats them like הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we no longer need the הרהור reading. רבי יהודה can require a בעל קרי to immerse and still let him say these ברכות, because they are not in the same group as ordinary Torah learning. The גמרא will now bring a source that explains what this group is.

keyTerms.meaning: He made them, he treated them as
The laws of proper conduct and good manners

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂאָן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ.
phrases.english: רבי יהודה made them like the laws of proper conduct.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the ברכות. The point is that a בעל קרי may say them, just as some allow him to learn הלכות דרך ארץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: עֲשָׂאָן רַבִּי יְהוּדָה כְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after the קשיא in step 3 knocked out the הרהור reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: Putting the ברכות in a different category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה must mean only הרהור
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say the ברכות out loud, because he treats them like הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי יהודה can be strict about immersing and still allow the ברכות to be said out loud.

steps.title: Torah must be learned with awe, as at Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a ברייתא that compares learning Torah in every generation to standing at חורב. Just as Sinai was with awe, fear, quaking and trembling, Torah learning must be that way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,' and right after it is written, 'the day you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב.' Just as there it was with awe, fear, quaking and trembling, so too here it must be with awe, fear, quaking and trembling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to explain רב נחמן בר יצחק's idea. It starts with a דרשה that connects teaching Torah to the experience at Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים come one right after the other, so the ברייתא learns that Torah learning must have the same awe that was felt at חורב. This sets up the reason a בעל קרי is kept away from Torah learning. The ברייתא continues in the next lines and will show which areas are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall make them known
Just as there... so too here

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: and it is written right after it:

phrases.aramaic: ״יוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַדְתָּ לִפְנֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּחוֹרֵב״,
phrases.english: 'The day that you stood before ה׳ your God at חורב,'
phrases.notes: דברים 4:10

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן בְּאֵימָה וּבְיִרְאָה וּבִרְתֵת וּבְזִיעַ,
phrases.english: just as there it was with awe, fear, quaking and trembling,
phrases.notes: 'There' means at Sinai. 'Here' means teaching Torah to your children.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן בְּאֵימָה וּבְיִרְאָה וּבִרְתֵת וּבְזִיעַ.
phrases.english: so too here it must be with awe, fear, quaking and trembling.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: ״וְהוֹדַעְתָּם לְבָנֶיךָ וְלִבְנֵי בָנֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that explains רב נחמן בר יצחק's comparison to הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.raayaObject: The background for רב נחמן בר יצחק's idea that some areas of learning are treated differently for a בעל קרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads דברים 4:9-10 together

steps.title: Severely impure people may learn Torah, but a man who had a seminal emission may not
steps.stepSummary: Based on the Sinai comparison, the ברייתא rules that זבים, מצורעים and those who had relations with a נדה may learn every part of Torah. A בעל קרי may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: זבים, מצורעים and men who had relations with a נדה may read תורה, נביאים and כתובים, and may learn משנה, גמרא, הלכות and אגדות. But men who had a קרי are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now draws its practical rule from the Sinai comparison. It lists who may learn Torah while impure and who may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Surprisingly, the people with the more severe טומאה are allowed to learn. Only the בעל קרי is forbidden. The rule comes from the Sinai comparison: Torah must be learned with awe, as at Sinai. The ברייתא itself does not say why קרי in particular is singled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Men with a special bodily discharge that makes them severely impure
People with צרעת, the skin disease of the Torah
Men who had relations with a woman who is a נדה
Men who had a seminal emission

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the stricter טומאה gets the stricter rule. Here the opposite is true: the severely impure may learn, and only the בעל קרי is held back.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole question of how far the ban on a בעל קרי reaches. The next opinions argue about exactly that.

phrases.english: From here they said:
phrases.notes: 'From here' points back to the Sinai comparison: Torah must be learned with awe and trembling, just like at Sinai.

phrases.english: Zavim and lepers
and those who have relations with menstruating women —
are permitted to read in the Torah
and in the Prophets and in the Writings,
and to study Mishnah and Gemara
and halachot and aggadot.
But those who had a seminal emission are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical ruling from the Sinai comparison in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Severely impure people may learn all Torah; a בעל קרי may not.

steps.title: Three opinions on how much a man with a seminal emission may learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי, רבי יונתן בן יוסף and רבי נתן בן אבישלום each allow a bit more learning than the one before.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says he may review the משניות he already knows, as long as he does not go deep into a משנה. רבי יונתן בן יוסף says he may go deep into the משנה but not into the גמרא. רבי נתן בן אבישלום says he may even go deep into the גמרא, as long as he does not say the names of ה׳ in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now lists opinions on exactly where the ban on a בעל קרי stops. Each of these three opinions is more lenient than the one before it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of it as a ladder. רבי יוסי allows only reviewing familiar material. רבי יונתן בן יוסף adds deep study of משנה. רבי נתן בן אבישלום adds deep study of גמרא, and only forbids saying ה׳'s names.

keyTerms.meaning: Material a person is used to and already knows
Lay out and explain in depth

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
He may study the familiar material,
phrases.notes: He means משניות the person already knows well and is just reviewing.

phrases.english: as long as he does not expound the Mishnah.
phrases.notes: Literally 'spread out': he may not open up a משנה and go into it in depth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yonatan ben Yosef says:
He may expound the Mishnah,
but he may not expound the Gemara.
Rabbi Natan ben Avishalom says:
He may even expound the Gemara,
as long as he does not say the mentions of God's name in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹנֶה הוּא בָּרְגִילִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the limits of the ban on a בעל קרי stated in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Graded opinions: review only; deep study of משנה; deep study of גמרא without ה׳'s names.

steps.title: The strictest view: no study of מדרש, or not even entering the study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, quoting רבי עקיבא, says a בעל קרי may not enter מדרש at all. Another version says he may not even enter the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, a student of רבי עקיבא, says in רבי עקיבא's name: he may not enter into מדרש at all. Some say the wording is: he may not enter the בית המדרש at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the strictest opinion. It also gives two versions of what that opinion actually said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In one version he is barred from מדרש, meaning explaining the פסוקים. In the other version he is barred from even walking into the בית המדרש. Either way, this is much stricter than the three opinions before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Explaining and drawing teachings out of the פסוקים

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan the Sandal-maker,
the student of Rabbi Akiva,
says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
He may not enter into midrash at all.
And some say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִכָּנֵס לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: He may not enter the study hall at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the strictest opinion to the list in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל קרי may not engage in מדרש at all (or, in the other version, may not enter the בית המדרש).

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows a man with a seminal emission to learn הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a בעל קרי may learn הלכות דרך ארץ. This is the source behind רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: he may learn הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line the גמרא was quoting the ברייתא for. רבי יהודה allows a בעל קרי to learn הלכות דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4, רב נחמן בר יצחק said that רבי יהודה lets a בעל קרי say ברכות out loud because he treats them like הלכות דרך ארץ. Here is the ברייתא showing that רבי יהודה does allow a בעל קרי to learn הלכות דרך ארץ. So the answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws of proper conduct and manners

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה allows a בעל קרי to learn הלכות דרך ארץ. That is why he also lets him say ברכות out loud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may study the laws of proper conduct.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שׁוֹנֶה הוּא בְּהִלְכוֹת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 5, giving the source for step 4.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that רבי יהודה treats ברכות like הלכות דרך ארץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement of רבי יהודה that a בעל קרי may learn הלכות דרך ארץ

steps.title: רבי יהודה immerses before teaching, being strict on himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה had a קרי, but before teaching הלכות דרך ארץ he went down into the river and immersed. He explained that he is lenient for others but strict with himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once רבי יהודה had a קרי and was walking along the river. His students said: Rebbe, teach us a chapter of הלכות דרך ארץ. He went down, immersed, and taught them. They said: Didn't you teach us that a בעל קרי may learn הלכות דרך ארץ? He said: Even though I am lenient for others, I am strict with myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי יהודה acting on his own rule. His students are surprised that he immersed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students' question shows that everyone knew רבי יהודה's rule was lenient. His answer does not take back the rule. It is only his personal choice to be stricter with himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A story about something that happened
Immersed in water to become טהור

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה did not change his ruling. The law for everyone stays lenient. Only he himself acted strictly.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabbi Yehuda, who had a seminal emission,
and he was walking along the riverbank.
His students said to him:
Our teacher, teach us one chapter
of the laws of proper conduct.
He went down, immersed, and taught them.
phrases.notes: He went down into the river they were walking beside.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Did you not teach us this, our teacher:
'He may study the laws of proper conduct'?!
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּיקֵל אֲנִי עַל אֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: Even though I am lenient with others,
I am strict with myself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁרָאָה קֶרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי יהודה himself acted on the rule from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה's lenient rule stands for others; he personally acted strictly.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: words of Torah cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה בן בתירא's view that Torah cannot become impure. So even an impure person may learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירא used to say: words of Torah do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, very lenient opinion on learning while impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier opinions put some limit on a בעל קרי. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says the Torah itself can never be made impure. So there is no reason to stop an impure person from learning.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הָיָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira would say:
Words of Torah do not become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הָיָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new, lenient view, unlike the restrictions listed in steps 6–9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Words of Torah cannot become impure, so impure people may learn.

steps.title: A student mumbles his learning and is told to speak clearly
steps.stepSummary: A student was mumbling his learning in front of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He was told to open his mouth, because Torah cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once a student was mumbling in front of רבי יהודה בן בתירא. He said to him: My son, open your mouth and let your words shine, because words of Torah do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story where רבי יהודה בן בתירא puts his rule into practice. It is setting up the פסוק that proves the rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The student was afraid to say Torah clearly while impure, so he mumbled. רבי יהודה בן בתירא told him there is nothing to fear. Torah cannot become impure, so he should say it out loud.

phrases.english: There was an incident with one student
who was mumbling
in front of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.
He said to him: My son,
open your mouth and let your words shine,
for words of Torah do not become impure,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּתַלְמִיד אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מְגַמְגֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יהודה בן בתירא applying his rule from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An impure student should say his Torah clearly, since Torah cannot become impure.

steps.title: Torah is like fire, and fire cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The rule is proven from a פסוק that compares ה׳'s word to fire. Fire cannot become impure, so Torah cannot either.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Is not My word like fire, says ה׳." Just as fire does not become impure, so too words of Torah do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בן בתירא gives the source for his rule: a פסוק that compares Torah to fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by comparison. Fire can never become impure. The פסוק calls ה׳'s word fire, so Torah shares that quality and cannot become impure either.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בתירא: Torah is like fire, and fire cannot become impure. So an impure person may say words of Torah out loud.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"Is not My word like fire, says the Lord",
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 23:29

phrases.english: just as fire does not become impure,

phrases.aramaic: אַף דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵינָן מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה.
phrases.english: so too words of Torah do not become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: הֲלֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule stated in steps 11–12.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה בן בתירא's rule that Torah cannot become impure
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 23:29, which compares ה׳'s word to fire

steps.title: The ברייתא's line supports רבי אלעאי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that a בעל קרי may explain משנה in depth but not גמרא, and shows that רבי אלעאי's ruling in the name of רב matches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: He may explain the משנה in depth but not the גמרא. This supports רבי אלעאי, who said in the name of רב, through רבי אחא בר יעקב: The הלכה is that he may explain the משנה in depth but not the גמרא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks one line from the ברייתא and points out that an אמורא, רבי אלעאי, rules exactly the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא drew a line: a בעל קרי may explain משנה in depth but not גמרא. רבי אלעאי, quoting רב, gives that same line as the final הלכה. So the ברייתא backs up his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Lays out and explains in depth (not just reviewing)
"This supports him." A source backs up someone's view.
"Our teacher." Here it refers to רב.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא quoted earlier about what a בעל קרי may learn.

phrases.english: He may expound the Mishna
but he may not expound the Gemara.
This supports Rabbi El'ai,
since Rabbi El'ai said
that Rabbi Acha bar Yaakov said
in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" here means רב.

phrases.english: The halacha is: he may expound the Mishna
but he may not expound the Gemara.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר. מַצִּיעַ אֶת הַמִּשְׁנָה וְאֵינוֹ מַצִּיעַ אֶת הַגְּמָרָא. מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אִלְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to a line in the earlier ברייתא after the side discussion about רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעאי's ruling (in the name of רב) that a בעל קרי may review משנה but not גמרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's statement: מציע את המשנה ואינו מציע את הגמרא

steps.title: The same question is a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this question is a dispute among תנאים. רבי מאיר allows משנה but not גמרא. רבי יהודה בן גמליאל, quoting רבי חנינא בן גמליאל, forbids both, and another version says he permits both.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a dispute of תנאים: He may explain the משנה in depth but not the גמרא; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: Both are forbidden. Some say he said: Both are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three positions on what a בעל קרי may learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds the middle view, the same as רבי אלעאי. The second opinion comes to us in two opposite versions: both forbidden, or both permitted. So there are three possible positions: middle, strict, and lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: "Like the תנאים." This question is already a dispute among תנאים.
Both this and that are forbidden
Both this and that are permitted

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of Tannaim:
He may expound the Mishna
but he may not expound the Gemara;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel:
Both this and that are forbidden.
And some say he said: Both this and that are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי אלעאי's view matches רבי מאיר's, which is one side of a dispute among תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a בעל קרי may explain משנה in depth but not גמרא. רבי יהודה בן גמליאל: both forbidden, or in another version, both permitted.

steps.title: Linking the two versions to earlier opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the strict version (both forbidden) follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, and the lenient version (both permitted) follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who said both are forbidden follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. The one who said both are permitted follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא matches each version of the second opinion to an opinion we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient version fits רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who taught that Torah cannot become impure (Steps 11-13). The strict version fits רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who forbids a בעל קרי from learning. So each version has a known authority behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: "The one who said." Used to refer back to a specific opinion.

phrases.english: The one who said both this and that are forbidden
follows Rabbi Yochanan the Sandal-maker;
the one who said both this and that are permitted
follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר זֶה וָזֶה אָסוּר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two versions of the second opinion in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both forbidden follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. Both permitted follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

steps.title: Practice follows three elders
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that common practice follows three elders: רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז, רבי יאשיה on כלאים, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא on Torah learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The world's practice follows these three elders: רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז, רבי יאשיה on כלאים, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא on words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the practical bottom line. On Torah learning, practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, so a בעל קרי may learn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the dispute about a בעל קרי on the lenient side: Torah cannot become impure. He also lists two more topics where practice follows a single elder. The גמרא will now explain each of the three.

keyTerms.meaning: "The world is accustomed." This is the common practice.
The first wool shearing, which is given to a כהן
Forbidden mixtures (of seeds, animals, or fabrics)
Words of Torah, meaning Torah learning

steps.whatToRemember: The final practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא: Torah cannot become impure, so a בעל קרי may learn Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה: a בעל קרי is not stopped from Torah learning.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The common practice follows these three elders:
like Rabbi El'ai about the first shearing,
like Rabbi Yoshiya about forbidden mixtures,

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira about words of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: נְהוּג עָלְמָא כְּהָנֵי תְּלָת סָבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the opinions in Steps 15-16 in favor of רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא: a בעל קרי may learn Torah. Practice also follows רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז and רבי יאשיה on כלאים.

steps.title: The source for רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind the first elder: רבי אלעאי says ראשית הגז applies only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז, as it was taught: רבי אלעאי says, ראשית הגז applies only in the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the three elders one at a time, beginning with רבי אלעאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעאי holds that the מצוה to give the first shearing to a כהן applies only in ארץ ישראל. So outside ארץ ישראל, people do not give it, and that is the common practice.
steps.confusionAlert: This רבי אלעאי is a תנא quoted in a ברייתא. He is not the רבי אלעאי from Step 14, an אמורא who quoted רב.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi El'ai about the first shearing:
as it was taught: Rabbi El'ai says:
The first shearing
applies only in the Land.
phrases.notes: "The Land" means ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי בְּרֵאשִׁית הַגֵּז דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first of the three elders listed in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The practice following רבי אלעאי on ראשית הגז
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי אלעאי says ראשית הגז applies only in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: The source for the second elder: רבי יאשיה on mixed seeds in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the source for the second elder. רבי יאשיה holds that a person is only liable for כלאי הכרם if he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed in one hand motion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The second elder is רבי יאשיה, on the topic of כלאים. The Torah says: 'Do not sow your vineyard with mixed seeds.' רבי יאשיה says a person is never liable until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed all in one throw of the hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list from step 17. It now shows the source for the second elder, רבי יאשיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יאשיה reads the פסוק narrowly. Liability only comes when two kinds of grain are sown together with the grape seed, all in one motion. This is a lenient view, and people's practice followed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures, here mixing seeds in a vineyard

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yoshiya regarding mixed species,
as it is written: "You shall not sow your vineyard with mixed seeds,"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:9

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya says: one is never liable
until he sows wheat, barley, and a grape seed
with one throw of the hand.
phrases.notes: He means all three go into the ground together, in a single motion.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה בְּכִלְאַיִם, כְּדִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources begun in step 18, moving to the second elder.
steps.raayaObject: That common practice follows רבי יאשיה on כלאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's reading of 'לֹא תִזְרַע כַּרְמְךָ כִּלְאָיִם'

steps.title: The source for the third elder: words of Torah cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא behind the third elder. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says that דברי תורה do not become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The third elder is רבי יהודה בן בתירא, on the topic of Torah learning. A ברייתא teaches that he says: words of Torah do not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of three elders. It shows the source for רבי יהודה בן בתירא's lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since Torah cannot become impure, a בעל קרי may learn and say Torah words. This is the lenient version from step 16, and step 17 said practice follows it.
steps.whatToRemember: Practice follows three lenient elders: רבי אלעאי (ראשית הגז only in ארץ ישראל), רבי יאשיה (כלאים only with wheat, barley and grape seed together), and רבי יהודה בן בתירא (Torah cannot become impure).

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira regarding words of Torah,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Words of Torah do not become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of three elders with the third source.
steps.raayaObject: That common practice follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא on Torah learning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה

steps.title: זעירי reports that a practice was abolished, in two versions
steps.stepSummary: זעירי reports that they abolished immersion. Another version says he reported that they abolished hand-washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: When זעירי came to בבל, he said: 'They abolished the immersion.' Some say he said: 'They abolished the hand-washing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short report from זעירי about how practice changed. This sets up the next step, which explains each version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two versions of what זעירי said. One says the טבילה of a בעל קרי was dropped. The other says the washing of hands before prayer was dropped.

phrases.english: When Ze'iri came, he said:
They abolished the immersion.
And some say: they abolished the hand-washing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא זְעֵירִי, אֲמַר: בַּטְּלוּהָ לִטְבִילוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the lenient ruling of רבי יהודה בן בתירא with a report about actual practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A practice was abolished: either the immersion of a בעל קרי, or hand-washing.

steps.title: Explaining each version of זעירי's report
steps.stepSummary: The 'immersion' version follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The 'hand-washing' version matches רב חסדא, who cursed anyone who goes searching for water at prayer time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever says 'they abolished immersion' is following רבי יהודה בן בתירא. Whoever says 'they abolished hand-washing' is following רב חסדא, who cursed a person who goes searching for water when it is time to pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each version of זעירי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The immersion version fits רבי יהודה בן בתירא: Torah cannot become impure, so a בעל קרי does not need טבילה to learn. The hand-washing version fits רב חסדא: you should not delay your prayer to hunt for water.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב חסדא is against washing hands. He only cursed someone who goes out of his way to look for water, and so misses the time for prayer.

phrases.english: The one who says they abolished the immersion
follows Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.
The one who says they abolished the hand-washing
follows this: that Rav Chisda cursed
anyone who goes searching for water at the time of prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בַּטְּלוּהָ לִטְבִילוּתָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind both versions of זעירי's report from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immersion version: follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא. Hand-washing version: follows רב חסדא's curse on searching for water at prayer time.

steps.title: Nine קבין of water poured over a בעל קרי makes him pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a בעל קרי who has nine קבין of water poured over him is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a בעל קרי who had nine קבין of water poured on him is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with an easier way for a בעל קרי to become pure, instead of full immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually purity requires going into a מקוה. Here, pouring nine קבין of water over him is enough to make him pure for learning and prayer. This is another leniency for the בעל קרי.

keyTerms.meaning: Nine kav, a measure of water

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling lets a בעל קרי avoid going to a מקוה. The next steps describe how it was passed along.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A בעל קרי
who had nine kav of water poured on him
is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בַּעַל קֶרִי שֶׁנָּתְנוּ עָלָיו תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another leniency on the topic of immersion for a בעל קרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine קבין of water poured over a בעל קרי make him pure.

steps.title: How the nine-קבין ruling was passed down
steps.stepSummary: נחום איש גם זו whispered the ruling to רבי עקיבא, who whispered it to בן עזאי. בן עזאי went out and taught it to his students in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחום איש גם זו whispered this ruling to רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא whispered it to בן עזאי. בן עזאי went out and taught it to his students in the marketplace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story of how the nine-קבין ruling was handed down from teacher to student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two teachers only whispered it, so it was kept quiet. בן עזאי then taught it openly in public. That is a big change in how the ruling was shared.

phrases.aramaic: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ לְחָשָׁהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Nachum of Gam Zo whispered it to Rabbi Akiva,
and Rabbi Akiva whispered it to Ben Azzai,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן עַזַּאי יָצָא וּשְׁנָאָהּ לְתַלְמִידָיו בְּשׁוּק.
phrases.english: and Ben Azzai went out and taught it to his students in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: נַחוּם אִישׁ גַּם זוֹ לְחָשָׁהּ לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes how the ruling of step 23 was handed down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling was whispered from teacher to student until בן עזאי taught it in public.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree: did בן עזאי teach it openly or whisper it?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא disagree about the end of the story. One says בן עזאי taught it openly, and the other says he whispered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל disagree about this: רבי יוסי בר אבין and רבי יוסי בר זבידא. One teaches that בן עזאי 'taught it.' The other teaches that he 'whispered it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a disagreement about the correct wording of the story's ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether בן עזאי made the ruling public, or kept it quiet like his teachers did. One version says 'שְׁנָאָהּ', he taught it openly. The other says 'לְחָשָׁהּ', he also only whispered it.
steps.whatToRemember: The nine-קבין leniency for a בעל קרי was handed down quietly. It is disputed whether בן עזאי made it public or also only whispered it.

phrases.english: Two Amoraim in the West disagree about it,
phrases.notes: "The West" means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר זְבִידָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin and Rabbi Yosei bar Zevida.
One teaches: "he taught it,"
and one teaches: "he whispered it."

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the last line of step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One version: בן עזאי taught it openly. The other version: he whispered it.

steps.title: Why one version says openly and the other says whispered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the reason behind each version of how בן עזאי taught the lenient ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says בן עזאי taught it openly holds that strict immersion rules would cause people to stop learning Torah and stop having children. The one who says he whispered it holds that he kept it quiet so Torah scholars would not be with their wives too often, like roosters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each side of the argument from the last step: why teach it openly, and why only whisper it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If immersion is hard, a בעל קרי might skip learning Torah or avoid being with his wife, so teaching the easy ruling openly helps. On the other side, if purifying is too easy, scholars might be with their wives all the time and lose focus on learning. So a quiet ruling keeps a natural limit in place.

phrases.english: The one who teaches "he taught it openly"
phrases.notes: This goes back to the two versions about בן עזאי in the last step.

phrases.english: it is because of neglect of Torah
and because of neglect of having children.
And the one who teaches "he whispered it"
holds it was so that Torah scholars should not be
constantly with their wives like roosters.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּתָנֵי שְׁנָאָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind each side of the disagreement in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teaching openly prevents neglect of Torah and of having children. Whispering prevents scholars from being with their wives too often.

steps.title: Some are lenient and some are strict, and the strict get long life
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי reports that there are both lenient and strict practices about this immersion, and praises the strict ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי said: I heard that some are lenient about this immersion and some are strict. Whoever is strict on himself gets a long life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי says the practice was never settled one way. He adds that being strict on yourself brings a blessing of long life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not decide the law for everyone. Instead he treats the strict way as an extra personal choice that is rewarded, not as an obligation on everyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai said:
I heard that people are lenient about it
phrases.notes: "It" means the immersion of a בעל קרי.

phrases.english: and I heard that people are strict about it,
and anyone who is strict about it on himself
his days and years are lengthened.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמְּקִילִּין בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of בן עזאי to a general statement about practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are both lenient and strict practices, and one who is strict on himself is blessed with long life.

steps.title: What is the point of those who immerse in the morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי seems to question the people who immerse in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is the point of those who immerse in the morning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי asks a question that sounds like he does not see the value in morning immersion. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, it sounds like he thinks a בעל קרי does not need to immerse at all. The גמרא will soon show that this simple reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: What is their point / what is their nature
Those who immerse in the morning

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is the point of those who immerse in the morning?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה טִּיבָן שֶׁל טוֹבְלֵי שְׁחָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another Amora's view about morning immersion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע בן לוי questions the value of morning immersion. Its meaning is clarified below.

steps.title: But he himself forbids a בעל קרי to learn Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the question of רבי יהושע בן לוי, because he himself requires purity before learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can he ask "what is their point"? He is the one who said that a בעל קרי is forbidden to learn Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the simple reading of רבי יהושע בן לוי's words. It says they contradict another ruling of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a בעל קרי may not learn Torah until he purifies himself, then the morning immersion has a clear purpose. So רבי יהושע בן לוי cannot be mocking it.

keyTerms.meaning: But he is the one who said
Words of Torah, meaning Torah learning

phrases.english: "What is their point"?!
But he is the one who said
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said this earlier in the סוגיא.

phrases.english: a בעל קרי is forbidden in words of Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה טִּיבָן הָא אִיהוּ דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the simple reading of step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement of רבי יהושע בן לוי questioning morning immersion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He elsewhere forbids a בעל קרי from learning Torah, so he must see a purpose in purifying. He cannot be dismissing it.

steps.title: He meant that a smaller amount of water or pouring is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יהושע בן לוי only questioned the need for a full מקוה and full immersion, not purification itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: Why use forty סאה when nine קבין is enough? Why immerse when pouring water is enough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by re-reading his words. He is not against purifying. He only says a full מקוה is not necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purification is still needed before learning Torah, so his two rulings fit together. His point is only about how to purify: nine קבין poured over the body works, as the ברייתא in step 23 taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty סאה, the amount of water for a מקוה
Nine קבין, a much smaller amount of water

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי agrees a בעל קרי must purify himself. He only holds that nine קבין, even poured, is enough instead of a full מקוה.

phrases.english: This is what he means:
what is the point of forty סאה,
when it is possible with nine קבין?
What is the point of immersing,
when it is possible with pouring?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר מַה טִּיבָן בְּאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the statement to narrow its meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He seemed to say that morning immersion has no purpose at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only means a full מקוה and immersion are unnecessary, since nine קבין poured over the body is enough.

steps.title: The full מקוה requirement was a great fence
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the requirement to immerse in forty סאה served as a strong protection against sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: They made a great fence with this rule.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא explains why the strict requirement of a full מקוה is valuable. The next step brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a smaller amount of water could work, the hard requirement kept people from sinning. That gives a reason for the strict practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A great fence, meaning a protective rule
They fenced, they set up a protection

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
They made a great fence with it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the requirement to immerse in forty סאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדֵר גָּדוֹל גָּדְרוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for the full מקוה, in contrast to the lenient view of step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forty סאה requirement acts as a powerful protection against sin.

steps.title: The woman who asked about forty סאה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a man who backed off from sinning once he was reminded he would need a full מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A man asked a woman to sin with him. She said: Empty one! Do you have forty סאה to immerse in? He backed off right away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to prove רבי חנינא's point that the full מקוה requirement stopped people from sinning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just being reminded of the hard immersion was enough to stop the man. This shows in real life how the strict rule worked as a fence.
steps.whatToRemember: The strict forty סאה requirement, even if not strictly needed, protected people from sin.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
There was an incident with a man
who asked a woman to sin with him.
She said to him: Empty one!
Do you have forty סאה
to immerse yourself in?
Immediately he backed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁתָּבַע אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חנינא's statement in step 31 with a story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that the forty סאה requirement is a great fence.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא telling of a man who stopped himself from sinning when reminded he would need forty סאה.

steps.title: רב הונא urges the חכמים not to neglect the immersion
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks the חכמים why they take this טבילה lightly, and says that if the cold is the problem, they can use heated bathhouses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to the חכמים: Gentlemen, why do you take this immersion lightly? If it is because of the cold, you can do it in the bathhouses.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes the חכמים to keep the immersion for a בעל קרי. He offers an easier option so the cold water will not stop them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the earlier steps showed how strong a protection this טבילה was, רב הונא sees people neglecting it. He guesses the reason is cold מקוה water. He suggests warm bathhouse water, which he holds is good enough for this special immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: taking lightly, treating without proper care

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to the Sages:
Gentlemen, for what reason
do you take this immersion lightly?
If it is because of the cold,
it is possible in the bathhouses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא לְרַבָּנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the importance of the immersion (steps 31-32) and offers a practical way to keep it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The immersion for a בעל קרי should not be neglected. Heated bathhouse water may be used for it.

steps.title: רב חסדא questions immersion in hot water
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges רב הונא: can a טבילה be done in hot water at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Is there such a thing as immersion in hot water?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on רב הונא's suggestion. He doubts that hot bathhouse water counts for an immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's whole solution depends on warm water being valid. רב חסדא attacks exactly that point. If hot water cannot purify, the bathhouse idea falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: "is it really so that...?" (opens a challenging question)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:
Is there then immersion in hot water?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי יֵשׁ טְבִילָה בְּחַמִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רב הונא's bathhouse suggestion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's suggestion to immerse in heated bathhouses
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טבילה may not work in hot water, so the bathhouse would not purify.

steps.title: רב הונא admits that רב אדא בר אהבה agrees with רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that רב אדא בר אהבה holds like רב חסדא, admitting there is an opinion against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רב אדא בר אהבה holds like you.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא responds by admitting that another great אמורא, רב אדא בר אהבה, shares רב חסדא's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not bring a proof that hot water works. He only admits that רב חסדא is not alone. The question about hot water stays as a real disagreement, and רב הונא keeps his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: holds like you, agrees with your opinion

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ.
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava holds like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה קָאֵי כְּווֹתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב חסדא's challenge by admitting that another sage agrees with him.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admission that the challenge reflects a real opinion, while the speaker keeps his own view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think רב חסדא's objection proves that hot water is clearly not valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a disagreement. רב אדא בר אהבה agrees with רב חסדא, but רב הונא still holds his position.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks for nine קבין to be poured on him
steps.stepSummary: While sitting in a tub of water in the bathhouse, רבי זירא tells his attendant to bring nine קבין of water and pour it over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא was sitting in a tub of water in the bathhouse. He said to his attendant: Go and bring me nine קבין and pour them over me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רבי זירא became pure. It sets up a question that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring תשעה קבין is the lighter way to become pure from קרי. The odd detail is that רבי זירא was already sitting in a tub of water, yet he still asked for water to be poured on him.

keyTerms.meaning: nine קב, the amount of water poured to become pure

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira was sitting
in a tub of water in the bathhouse.
He said to his attendant:
Go and bring me nine kav
and pour them over me.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי זֵירָא הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּאַגָּנָא דְמַיָּא בֵּי מַסּוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bathhouse immersion to the method of pouring nine קבין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי זירא acted on the view that he needed nine קבין poured over him, even while sitting in water.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא asks why pouring is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא asks רבי זירא why he needs all this, since he is already sitting in that much water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said to him: Why does the master need all this? He is already sitting in it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא challenges רבי זירא's behavior. He asks why pouring is needed when רבי זירא is already sitting in the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that what matters is the nine קבין of water touching the person. Sitting in a tub holding that much water should be just as good as having it poured on. So bringing more water looks pointless.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to him:
Why does the master need all this?
But he is sitting inside them!
phrases.notes: "Them" means the nine קבין.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמָר כּוּלֵּי הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי זירא's request from the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's request to have nine קבין poured over him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He is already sitting in at least nine קבין, so pouring more water seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Nine קבין works only by pouring, just as ארבעים סאה works only by immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא compares the two amounts: ארבעים סאה purifies only by immersion, and תשעה קבין purifies only by pouring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is like ארבעים סאה. Just as ארבעים סאה works by immersion and not by pouring, so too nine קבין works by pouring and not by immersion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains his behavior with a comparison. Each amount of water has its own fixed method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר אבא thought the amount of water was all that counted. רבי זירא shows that the method counts too. Sitting in nine קבין is not valid, because nine קבין must be poured, just as forty סאה must be immersed in.

keyTerms.meaning: forty סאה, the amount of water a מקוה needs
"just as... so too": the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: Each method of purifying has its own amount and its own way: ארבעים סאה only by immersion, תשעה קבין only by pouring. The two cannot be swapped.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that nine קבין is just a "small מקוה." It is a different method altogether. Sitting in nine קבין does nothing; it must be poured.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is like forty se'ah.
Just as forty se'ah
work by immersion and not by pouring,
so too nine kav
work by pouring and not by immersion.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּאַרְבָּעִים סְאָה, מָה אַרְבָּעִים סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חייא בר אבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison that shows each method only works in its own way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the amount of water matters, so sitting in nine קבין should be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: Nine קבין purifies only by pouring, just as forty סאה purifies only by immersion.

steps.title: רב נחמן prepares a nine-קב jug
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן set up a jug holding nine קבין so people could pour it over themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן prepared a jug that holds nine קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports a practical step: רב נחמן made the pouring method easy to use by preparing a jug of the right size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the nine-קב pouring method was really used in practice. Since nine קבין must be poured, a ready jug of that size made it simple. The next step will limit when this method may be used.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman prepared
a jug that holds nine kav.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן תַּקֵּן חַצְבָּא בַּת תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the pouring method by showing it used in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן made pouring nine קבין available by preparing a jug of that size.

steps.title: רב דימי limits the nine-קב leniency to a sick person with an involuntary emission
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה גלוסטרא that nine קבין was taught only for a sick person whose emission was involuntary. A sick person with a normal emission needs ארבעים סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: רבי עקיבא and רבי יהודה גלוסטרא said: This was taught only for a sick person whose emission was by accident. But a sick person whose emission was normal needs ארבעים סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a teaching from ארץ ישראל that narrows the nine-קב leniency. It does not apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now it seemed that anyone could use nine קבין, like with רב נחמן's jug. רב דימי says it was taught only for a sick person whose emission happened against his will. If the emission was normal, even a sick person must immerse in a full מקוה of ארבעים סאה.

keyTerms.meaning: when [he] came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: The pouring of תשעה קבין is a narrow leniency. It was taught only for a sick person with an involuntary emission. A normal emission requires ארבעים סאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit of the lighter method. It explains why the full מקוה stays the main requirement, which fits the earlier idea that the forty סאה served as a protection against sin.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה גְּלוֹסְטְרָא אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: he said: Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yehuda Gelostera said:
They taught this only for a sick person who had it by accident.
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule that pouring nine קבין is enough to become pure.

phrases.english: But for a sick person whose emission was the normal kind,
phrases.notes: "Normal" means the usual way, such as through marital relations, and not something that happened to him by accident.

phrases.english: forty se'ah are required.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the nine-קב method that was just shown in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nine קבין works only for a sick person with an involuntary emission. A sick person with a normal emission needs ארבעים סאה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב נחמן's jug is broken
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says that, after רב דימי's report, רב נחמן's nine-קבין jug is "broken." It is hardly useful anymore.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רב נחמן's jug is broken.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws a practical result from רב דימי's report. If nine קבין helps only a sick person with an involuntary emission, almost nobody can use רב נחמן's jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 39, רב נחמן set up a nine-קבין jug for everyone to pour over themselves. In Step 40, רב דימי limited nine קבין to one rare case: a sick person whose emission was involuntary. So רב יוסף says the jug is "broken." It still holds water, but now it serves almost no one.

keyTerms.meaning: a jug or large clay jar

steps.confusionAlert: The jug did not physically break. "Broken" is a figure of speech. It means the jug has lost its purpose.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rav Nachman's jug is broken.
phrases.notes: He means it is useless now, since only a rare sick person could rely on nine קבין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִתְּבַר חַצְבֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב דימי's limitation (Step 40) to רב נחמן's practice (Step 39) and shows that the practice has lost its purpose.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רב דימי's report, the nine-קבין jug is practically useless for most people.

steps.title: רבין arrives and begins reporting an incident in אושא
steps.stepSummary: רבין comes from ארץ ישראל and starts to tell of an incident that happened in אושא. The details come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: In אושא there was an incident.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבין is opening a story from אושא, and the גמרא will tell the actual details in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after רב יוסף declared the jug useless, a new report arrives from ארץ ישראל. Bringing a real incident (עובדא) at this point suggests it bears on the nine-קבין question. It may soften or push back on the conclusion that the jug is useless. We only find out how once the story is told.
